rules.statement: An avatar always resolves to a name in text nearby or in its accessible name; an image alone is never the only identification.

Initials are derived from the display name deterministically, capped at two graphemes, with a per-person colour chosen by hash rather than by mood; a missing image shows initials, never a broken icon.
Presence is a dot plus a text equivalent in the accessible name ('Amina Rahman, online'); colour alone never carries it.
Avatars ship at 24, 32 and 40 px with a 2 px ring on overlap; anything larger is a profile header, not an avatar.
A stack shows at most three faces plus a '+N' whose accessible name lists the remaining names, and the stack is not the only way to see membership.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a late-loading image replaces the initials only if the person is still the same; a stale response for a previous person is discarded

motion.motion: initials stay in place with no animation over 120ms
motion.reducedMotion: initials stay in place with no animation

motion.motion: the image cross-fades over 160ms over the initials
motion.reducedMotion: the image replaces the initials instantly

motion.motion: initials remain over 100ms while the failed image is dropped
initials stay while the retry runs for 120ms

transitions.trigger: the avatar's profile action is opened

motion.motion: the focus ring disappears with no delay
motion.reducedMotion: identical — the ring is immediate in both cases

motion.noneReason: unavailability is a permission or load fact, not an animation; the control states why instead of moving

sections.intent: Identify a person at a glance while always leaving a readable name behind the picture.
nicheDifferences: Avatars are decoration with a job: they accelerate recognition but never carry identity
Products that rely on the photo alone lock out anyone whose face is not their identifier
inputs: the display name's script and length
the sizes used in each surface
anatomy: an image with alt text equal to the name
a presence dot with a text equivalent
styling: 24/32/40 px ladder with a 2 px page-coloured ring on overlap
initials in the same weight as body text, never bold display type
presence dot is 8 px, bottom-right, with a ring
a11y: alt text is the person's name, or empty when the name is adjacent in text
presence is included in the accessible name, not only as colour
the stack's +N names the remaining people
the profile popover is a button with an accessible name
responsive: stacks drop from three faces to two below 480 px
the +N keeps its own label rather than shrinking to an unreadable badge
initials never wrap or scale down below 10 px
copy: initials come from the name, not the email local part
an offline person reads 'Amina Rahman, offline'
alternatives: a plain name link when the list is small and textual
a initials-only list for dense audit tables
a facepile with a membership link on click
acceptance: every avatar is identifiable by name in text or accessible name
a missing or failed image shows deterministic initials rather than a broken icon
presence is exposed as text as well as a dot
a stack of more than three shows a +N that names the rest
initials cap at two graphemes for any script
failureCases: the photo is the only identity and the name appears nowhere
initials are derived from an email address so they read as gibberish
presence is a green dot only
a 200 px avatar is used as an illustration

refused.reason: an avatar is either shown or absent; it has no inert state
a group summary is never rendered disabled
